questions.q: What does it mean for a pipeline to be idempotent?
options: Running it twice on the same input produces the same result as running it once — no duplicated rows, no doubled totals
It can only ever be run a single time, ever
It runs faster the second time it's executed
It automatically retries on failure with no other property
questions.explain: This matters because real jobs sometimes get retried, and a non-idempotent pipeline silently corrupts data on rerun.

questions.q: Why would mode("append") make a bronze-to-silver pipeline unsafe to rerun?
options: The same bronze batch processed twice would produce the same cleaned rows twice, duplicating data
append mode is not a valid write mode for Delta tables
append mode automatically deletes the target table first
There's no real risk; append is always safe to rerun
questions.explain: This is exactly the idempotency problem MERGE is designed to solve.

questions.q: How does MERGE make a silver pipeline idempotent?
options: Matching on a key used for deduplication, it only inserts genuinely new rows and updates existing ones instead of duplicating them
It deletes the entire table before every write
It ignores all incoming data on a rerun
It has no effect on idempotency; only append mode ensures that
questions.explain: This is the concrete mechanism (from Lesson 22) that makes rerunning the pipeline safe.

questions.q: What role do widgets play in a real bronze-to-silver pipeline?
options: They let a job supply which date/batch to process as a parameter, rather than someone typing it in by hand
They only matter for interactive, one-off exploration and have no role in a scheduled job
Widgets are used to define the Delta table's schema
Widgets replace the need for MERGE entirely
questions.explain: This directly reuses Lesson 9's widget/job-parameter mechanism from Chapter 1.

questions.q: What's the complete mechanical pattern a real bronze-to-silver pipeline follows?
options: A widget-driven date filter, reading from bronze, applying Lesson 27's transformations, and writing with MERGE — wrapped as a notebook attached to a scheduled job
A single SQL statement with no PySpark involved at all
Manually running Lesson 27's code by hand every day
A pipeline that reads directly from gold instead of bronze
questions.explain: This ties together widgets (Lesson 9), jobs (Lesson 11), and MERGE (Lesson 22) into one coherent pipeline.
